messages:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'eu-west-2-hotshot' SLO breach detected. p95 = 1.2s (baseline 120ms), p99 = 4.8s. Multiple streaming stalls > 20s. Queue depth spike observed. Paging @ashley (oncall).

ashley (oncall): acked. I'm on it, pulling dashboards now. Any realtime runbook pointers?

samuel (infra): seeing a sudden jump in warmup queue for that pool — warmup latency ~80-120s per slot, autoscaler see requests but scale-up handshake taking ~45-70s. Likely cold-slot warmup bottleneck + handshake backpressure.

jin (sre): +1. streaming tail latencies line up with queue depth > 300 and many requests hitting cold KV cache path (no prefix cached). Streaming stalls correlate with slot-init events.

ashley (oncall): quick customer impact -- cory, can you surface any CS tickets?

cory (support): flagged two customers (acct: acme-a, acct: bluefin) reporting timeouts and streaming stalls. Estimated affected: ~75 customers with degraded p95, 6 customers saw errors/timeouts.

samuel (infra): digging into autoscaler logs. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T12:08:14Z] scale_request id=sr-9f2 pool=eu-west-2-hotshot desired=+6 current=12
[2026-03-15T12:08:15Z] handshake start -> provisioning slot slot_id=x-27
[2026-03-15T12:09:02Z] slot ready -> runtime warmup start (kvcache mismatch)
[2026-03-15T12:09:50Z] runtime warmup complete -> slot join OK
[2026-03-15T12:09:55Z] slot accepted traffic -> immediate backpressure observed
```
Looks like effective provisioning time ~70s plus warmup ~40-60s in some cases. Combined adds ~2m before capacity is usable.

jin (sre): mitigation proposals: 1) enable routing policy fallback to model-variant-small for non-SLAd customers; 2) temporarily reduce batch size / concurrency for streaming to avoid head-of-line blocking; 3) kick autoscaler to use hot-standby slots (if we can) or pre-warm minimal set.

maria (platform): we have a prewarm knob on the pool (prewarm_count) but it's currently 0 for cost reasons. I can flip prewarm_count=2 for eu-west-2-hotshot for next 10m to absorb spikes. That reduces cold starts but increases cost.

ashley (oncall): do it. maria, flip prewarm now. jin, can you apply routing fallback? samuel, keep watching scale events. I'll update execs and CS.

maria (platform): toggled prewarm_count -> 2 (effective immediately). UI shows two slots spinning up.

samuel (infra): manually triggered scale request with override to allow immediate slot allocation (temp-override=true). Watching handshake events.

ashley (oncall): applying routing fallback to route "best-effort" customers to model-variant-small: 
```json
{"policy":"route_fallback","pool":"eu-west-2-hotshot","fallback":"model-variant-small","target":"non-SLA","duration":"15m"}
```
done.

ops-bot: NOTE: Routing change pushed by ashley (oncall) at 12:12:30Z. Prewarm slots creating. Autoscaler override requested.

jin (sre): immediate telemetry: queue depth falling from 420 -> 90 over 3 minutes, p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 320ms, p99 now ~980ms. Streaming stall events dropping.

cory (support): CS update posted to affected customers. Two high-touch accounts in retry/backoff. No SLA credits yet but we flagged for incident review.

ashley (oncall): good. I'll keep thread open for 30m then handoff to jin for post-incident. Current timeline: breach window started 12:08Z, mitigations in place 12:12Z, p99 improved by 12:16Z.

samuel (infra): root-cause hypothesis: sudden traffic burst triggered cold-scale path; autoscaler handshake + runtime warmup + kvcache cold path combined to create >2m effective cold ramp. Also see a small regression in new kernel selection that extended warmup by ~10-20s for certain models (investigating).

jin (sre): immediate follow-ups for postmortem: - autoscaler: evaluate handshake latency and add telemetry to break down schedule->provision->warmup times - platform: consider small always-on prewarm for hotshot pools or dynamic prewarm heuristics - runtime: investigate kernel selection regression that extended warmup for model family x-series

maria (platform): noted. I'll open tickets and schedule a config experiment: dynamic prewarm when queue_depth > 50 for 3 consecutive min.

ashley (oncall): handing off to jin (sre) at 12:32Z. Summary: dedicated pool saturated by burst, autoscaler and warmup delay caused SLO breaches. Mitigations applied: fallback routing (non-SLA -> smaller model), prewarm_count=2, autoscaler override. Customer impact: ~75 customers degraded, 6 timeouts, 2 escalations to CS.

jin (sre): ack takeover. I'll run follow-up triage and coordinate postmortem and timeline. Next actions: collect full traces for 12:00-12:40Z, gather autoscaler logs, list impacted customers + token-level traces (redact PII), and prepare RCA draft.

ops-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> mitigated. Monitoring window open for 60m. Please add incident tag and link to playback.

ashley (oncall): :white_check_mark: closing my active pager. Leaving notes in pager duty and tagging platform + autoscaler teams.

cory (support): customers notified and weekly exec summary updated.

jin (sre): will follow up with an RFC for prewarm heuristics and autoscaler handshake improvements. Assigning owners in next hour.

ops-bot: Incident timeline recorded. Please update with any further regressions.
